---
title: "Study 02 — Periodicity & temperature"
subtitle: "(H₂O)₈ periodic (GFN1) · trimer temperature sweep"
---

## Confinement fixes evaporation

An 8-water periodic box stays condensed for the whole run (max O–O oscillates
6–7 Å, never leaves the cell) while the gas-phase cluster separates past 100 Å.
**Periodicity removes the evaporation channel** — though it forces GFN1, since
GFN2 has no PBC multipoles in this build, so gas (GFN2) and periodic (GFN1)
results are not at the same level of theory.

![Periodic box stays bounded (≤ 7.7 Å); the gas-phase cluster
evaporates past 100 Å.](assets/pbc_vs_gas.png){width=560}

## A big O–O gap is drift, not dissociation

A complementary CV pair resolves the ambiguity: checking the intramolecular O–H
shows the clusters are **intact molecules drifting apart**, not dissociating —
only the lone water truly breaks a bond. Higher temperature just makes intact
molecules escape faster (max O–O 81 → 143 Å over 200 → 350 K).

![Gas trimer: three intact waters drift to the corners, each keeping its two
O–H bonds — drift, not dissociation.](assets/movie_n3_low.gif){width=360}
